01 // ORIGIN & MISSION

FORGED IN THE LAB.
PROVEN IN THE ARENA.

Torque Crew is an independent competitive robotics team engineered to push beyond conventional limits. When the countdown starts, our alliance delivers.

Engineering With No Compromise

Founded on the principle of relentless engineering, Torque Crew was created to bridge high-level robotics theory with aggressive, real-world match performance. In HyperDrive, matches are won in milliseconds. We optimize every gram of weight, every line of computer vision code, and every driver reflex.

From rapid-prototyping in our CNC workshop to custom PCB routing and sensor fusion, every mechanism on our machine is designed for speed, torque, and survivability under competition collision.

"We don't build robots to participate. We build machines that redefine how HyperDrive matches are played."

TORQUE CREW // ROADMAP

THE JOURNEY SO FAR — AND WHAT COMES NEXT

TORQUE CREW didn't come together overnight.

INTRODUCTION

What started with a simple introduction to the National Robotics League slowly turned into a team, a plan, an identity, and a journey that is still unfolding.

This roadmap captures the important moments that have brought us here — and the milestones that are still ahead.

02 SEPTEMBER 2026 — THE BEGINNING

It all started with a call.

Our teacher introduced us to something we didn't know much about before — the National Robotics League.

At first, we were confused.

We didn't know exactly what the competition was about, what we would have to build, or what would be expected from us.

So we started researching.

The more we learned about NRL, the more interested we became. What began as confusion slowly turned into curiosity, and that curiosity turned into excitement.

That's when we made the decision:

We were going to participate.

This was the first step in the journey of TORQUE CREW.

EARLY SEPTEMBER — BUILDING THE TEAM

Once we decided to take part, we began figuring out how we would work together.

We discussed our strengths, responsibilities, and the different roles needed within the team.

Everyone started taking responsibility for a specific part of the journey.

This was when TORQUE CREW started becoming more than just a group of people — it started becoming a team.

EARLY SEPTEMBER — OUR IDENTITY TAKES SHAPE

After setting our team roles, we began working on something equally important:

Our identity.

We created the TORQUE CREW logo, giving our team a visual identity that represented who we were and what we wanted to build.

It became one of the first things that made TORQUE CREW feel real.

From that point forward, the name had a face.

06 SEPTEMBER 2026 — OUR FIRST SHOOT

Just a few days after everything began, we came together for our first reel shoot.

We planned the shots, worked together, filmed our content, and took our first step towards introducing TORQUE CREW to the public.

We didn't want the footage to simply stay on a camera roll.

So we published our reel on Instagram on the very same day.

It was a small step, but it marked the beginning of our presence beyond the team itself.

08 SEPTEMBER 2026 — OFFICIAL CREW INTRODUCTION

Our official TORQUE CREW introduction reel went live.

For the first time, we introduced the people behind the name — our members, roles, and responsibilities.

TORQUE CREW was no longer just an idea being discussed behind the scenes.

We were officially out there.

09–16 SEPTEMBER 2026 — PLANNING & BUILDING

The days that followed were about putting the foundation in place.

We continued with meetings, discussions, planning, and team coordination.

We worked on our ideas, responsibilities, content, and plans for the season.

There was still a lot to figure out, but every discussion helped us understand where we were going.

Step by step, the foundation of TORQUE CREW was being built.

17 SEPTEMBER 2026 — OUR WEBSITE LAUNCH

TORQUE CREW officially went online.

On 17 September, we launched our official team website.

The website became a place where our team, our people, our work, our story, and our journey could come together in one place.

But more importantly, it became a way for us to document this journey as it grows.

This website isn't the end result.

It's a record of everything that comes next.

NOW — PREPARING FOR WHAT'S AHEAD

Right now, our focus is not only on robotics.

Our exams are approaching, and academics come first.

Until our exams are completed, we will focus on our studies while continuing to keep the team organized and our plans ready.

Once our exams are over, we'll take a short 1–2 week break to recharge.

And then, the real work begins.

AFTER EXAMS — 10 DAYS OF INTENSIVE ROBOTICS

After our break, we'll have a 10-day holiday.

And that's when we plan to put serious time into robotics.

During these 10 days, TORQUE CREW will shift into intensive work mode.

We'll focus on:

  • Robot development
  • Mechanical work
  • Electrical systems
  • Programming
  • Testing
  • Strategy
  • Team coordination
  • Skill development
  • Improving our understanding of the competition

The goal is simple:

Use those 10 days to push ourselves as far as we can.

COMMUNITY OUTREACH — TAKING ROBOTICS BEYOND OUR TEAM

Our journey isn't going to stay inside our college or inside our workshop.

We have planned community outreach across three different schools.

We'll introduce students to robotics, interact with them, and work towards increasing awareness and interest in what we're doing.

For us, outreach isn't just about promoting TORQUE CREW.

It's about sharing the excitement of robotics with more people.

EXPLORA — ROBOTICS MEETS CAMPUS

Our college's Explora event will be another important milestone.

We've planned to conduct robotics-related games and activities during the event.

The idea is to make robotics interactive, competitive, and fun — giving more students an opportunity to experience something related to robotics themselves.

This will also give TORQUE CREW another opportunity to connect with our college community.

BRANDING — BUILDING THE TORQUE CREW IDENTITY

Alongside robotics, we're also planning a lot for our branding and team identity.

The logo was only the beginning.

As the journey continues, we'll be working on our visual identity, team presence, content, and other branding ideas that will help make TORQUE CREW recognizable.

Every detail matters — from how we present ourselves online to how we represent the team at events.

THE ROAD AHEAD

There is still a lot waiting for us.

More planning.

More building.

More testing.

More learning.

More outreach.

More ideas.

More problems to solve.

And, hopefully, many moments worth remembering.

What began with a teacher's call on 2 September has already become a team, a logo, a public identity, and an official website.

But those are only the first milestones.

The roadmap doesn't end here.

It continues with every meeting, every build, every failure, every improvement, every event, and every challenge we take on together.

Because TORQUE CREW isn't just preparing for a competition.

We're building the journey along the way.

ONE CREW. ONE DRIVE. ONE GOAL.
TORQUE CREW // OUR JOURNEY

IT ALL STARTED
WITH A CALL.

On 2 September 2026, our teacher called us and introduced us to something we hadn't really known much about before — the National Robotics League.

At first, we were confused.

We didn't really know what the competition was about, what we would have to do, what we were expected to build, or what this journey would eventually become.

But instead of simply leaving it there, we decided to learn more. We started researching the National Robotics League, understanding the competition, exploring what participation would involve, and discovering what was actually waiting for us.

The more we researched, the more interested we became. What started as confusion slowly turned into curiosity. And that curiosity eventually turned into excitement.

That's when we made our decision. We decided to participate.

02 SEPTEMBER — THE BEGINNING

This was the moment everything started.

We didn't have the complete plan. We didn't have every answer. We didn't know exactly how far this would take us.

But we had something important: a reason to start.

From that day, TORQUE CREW began taking shape.

06 SEPTEMBER — OUR FIRST SHOOT

Just a few days later, on 6 September, we came together for a reel shoot. The goal was simple — create something that would introduce our team and begin building our identity online.

We arrived, planned the shots, worked together, and filmed our content. It was one of our first experiences working together not just as individuals, but as TORQUE CREW.

And we didn't want the moment to sit on a camera roll. We finished the shoot and posted our reel on Instagram the very same day.

It might have been our first small step into the public eye, but to us, it meant something bigger. People could finally see the team beginning to come together.

IN BETWEEN — MEETINGS & TEAM BUILDING

Between the first shoot and our official introduction, we continued having several meetings.

We discussed ideas. We figured things out. We talked about our responsibilities and roles. We started understanding how we could work together effectively.

There was still a lot to learn, but every meeting brought us one step closer.

The team wasn't built in a single day. It was built through conversations, ideas, decisions, and the willingness to work together.

08 SEPTEMBER — OFFICIAL CREW INTRO

Then came 8 September. Our official TORQUE CREW introduction reel went live.

This wasn't just another post. It introduced the people behind the name — the members, the different roles, and the individuals who would be taking this journey forward together.

For the first time, we weren't just an idea or a team preparing behind the scenes. TORQUE CREW was officially out there.

And with that post, we could finally say: this is TORQUE CREW. And this is only the beginning.

NOW — THE JOURNEY CONTINUES

What you've seen so far is only the first few steps of our journey.

From a teacher's call on 2 September... to researching the National Robotics League... to deciding to take the challenge... to our first reel shoot on 6 September... to the meetings, planning, and teamwork in between... and finally, introducing the entire crew to the world on 8 September.

Every one of those moments is now part of our story. But the story doesn't end here. In fact — this is where it really begins.

There will be challenges. There will be things that don't go according to plan. There will be late discussions, new ideas, unexpected problems, testing, learning, building, improving, and hopefully moments that we'll look back on with pride.

And we're going to document it all. Because this isn't just about entering a robotics competition — it's about everything we learn and experience along the way. It's about becoming better as individuals. It's about learning how to work as one team. It's about turning ideas into something real. And most importantly, it's about the journey.
